lead.en: The view in {city} has outgrown my note slip.

text.zh-Hans: 我从清水寺的木舞台望向京都，想把远处的城装进一张便签。城太大，便签太小，最后只装下一个很努力的长方形。我把它留到离开寺院后才补画，明天看看能不能认出今天站的位置。
text.en: From Kiyomizu-dera’s wooden stage, I tried fitting Kyoto onto a note slip. The city proved larger than my stationery. For now there is one ambitious rectangle, filled in after I left the temple. Tomorrow I will see if I can find where I was standing.
Talk about what missed the page
Remember the view from the stage

lead.zh-Hans: {city}的声音，今天先用铅笔寄回来。
lead.en: Sending a sound from {city}, with some help from a pencil.

text.zh-Hans: 走过二条城二之丸御殿的廊道，脚下有细细的鸣响。离开后，我和一位同行的旅人各画了一条线，试着记下那个声音。我的线像一根面条，对方的像打了结的细绳。我们约好下次再比一比。
text.en: The corridor floor at Ninomaru Palace gave a little chirp underfoot. After leaving, another visitor and I each drew a line to remember the sound. Mine resembled a noodle; theirs looked like tangled string. We agreed the two drawings needed another meeting.
Ask for one more sound line
Compare the bends in the lines

lead.en: Taking my time with a menu sketch in {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 吃汤豆腐时，我先把蘸汁碟画在菜单边上，等锅里的豆腐温温地送到碗里。画完才发现，碟子比锅还大。也许这张菜单只是特别重视配角。明天再给小锅找个好位置。
text.en: Over yudofu, I sketched the dipping dish while the tofu warmed in its pot. On the finished menu the dish is larger than the pot. Perhaps my drawing has a soft spot for supporting characters. I will find the little pot a better seat tomorrow.
Discuss the star of the menu
Give pot and dish equal space

lead.zh-Hans: {city}的菜单里，多了一页薄薄的画。
lead.en: A delicate new page for my menu collection from {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 今天吃了汤叶，也就是豆浆加热后表面结出的薄膜。我在手绘菜单上画了一层又一层，后来才发现自己把它画成了叠好的信纸。倒也合适，我正想写一封薄薄的信。明天再给画里的信封找收件人。
text.en: Today I tried yuba, the thin skin lifted from heated soy milk. My menu drawing acquired so many layers that it began to resemble folded letter paper. Convenient: I was planning a very small letter. Tomorrow its sketched envelope will need an address.
Choose the drawn letter’s recipient
Look at the delicate layers

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，记声音的便签又长了一截。
lead.en: You wrote, “{reply}.” Our paper record of a sound has grown a little longer.

text.zh-Hans: 那位同行的旅人真的又添了一条线，把我们上次画的“面条”和“绳结”连在一起。我在旁边画了小小的邮包，给这张二条城记声音的纸一个寄信的位置。我们都没能画出声音，却多了一张舍不得折的便签。下次得带个宽一点的信封。
text.en: My fellow visitor added a line joining our old noodle and knot. I drew a tiny mailbag beside them, giving this paper memory of Nijo-jo somewhere to post a letter. Neither of us captured the chirp, but now neither wants to fold the drawing. Next time I will bring a wider envelope.
Bring a wider envelope next time
Find where the old lines meet

lead.en: Two menu sketches from a meal in {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 今天点了小份的汤豆腐，也尝了汤叶。我和邻座聊起两张手绘菜单，一张画锅和蘸碟，另一张画薄薄的豆浆皮。聊完才发现，两张纸被我挤在同一个信封里。我替它们分好座位，明天再来听它们说什么。
text.en: Today I had a small serving of yudofu and tried yuba too. Over a chat with my neighbour, I drew a pot and dipping dish on one menu and delicate soy-milk skin on another. Both pages ended up squeezed into one envelope. They have separate seats now; conversation can resume tomorrow.
Talk about the two menus
Compare the two sketches

lead.en: Two menu sketches from a meal in {city}.

text.zh-Hans: 午饭尝了汤豆腐和汤叶。一个在热汤里温着，一个薄得让我想起信纸，我慢慢画了两张菜单。蘸碟在纸上很安静，汤叶的线却有点歪。我把歪线留下，明天再看看它像什么。
text.en: Lunch was a little yudofu and yuba: tofu kept warm in broth, and a delicate skin that reminded me of letter paper. I took my time drawing two menus. The dipping dish sits very calmly; the yuba lines wander. I kept the wobbly one for tomorrow to explain.
Talk about the two menus
Compare the two sketches
